content.title: DataFest Africa 2025: Reclaiming Data Futures
content.summary: AKU, Pollicy unite innovators to shape ethical, people-centred digital systems

content.text: recently concluded the DataFest Africa 2025 - Nairobi Satellite Edition, a high-energy gathering that explored how African communities can reclaim their data futures and shape ethical, inclusive digital systems. Co-hosted with Pollicy (Uganda), the Nairobi programme combined lightning talks, a keynote panel, exhibitions and community dialogues to connect innovators, policymakers, researchers, creatives and grassroots changemakers under the theme "Reclaiming Our Data Futures."

The day's sessions made a clear case for people-centred data practice. Discussions on community-centred data infrastructure examined practical pathways to trusted, local data hubs; hands-on showcases at the Tech Garden and the interactive Data Museum translated complex ideas into tangible demos; and an inter-generational dialogue opened space for attendees to reflect on digital participation, privacy, AI literacy and mental wellbeing in the civic sphere. Attendees consistently emphasised that data collected in Africa should deliver value back to the communities who generate it and inform decisions in clinics, classrooms, cooperatives and county halls, not only in corporate dashboards or national portals.

The momentum generated in Nairobi will carry forward through a post-event agenda focused on collaboration and capacity building. The AKU Data Innovation Office is committed to nurturing inclusive, community-centred spaces like DataFest Africa, places where builders and users meet, where technology meets real stories, where critique is welcome, and where the point is not the splash but the sustainability of the solutions.

As noted by Professor Nancy Booker, Dean at AKU's Graduate School of Media and Communications, in her opening remarks at the festival; "Reclaiming our data futures means putting people before platforms. When communities can access, govern, and benefit from their own data, technology stops being extractive and becomes a public good. That is the future we're building from Nairobi outward; practical, ethical, and owned by the people it is meant to serve."

DataFest Africa 2025 - Nairobi affirmed that when technology, storytelling and social impact meet, data becomes a public good. Next stop the celebration continues across to Lira, Uganda (Northern Uganda) on 23 October, followed by Kampala on 30-31 October as DataFest Africa carries forward the momentum to scale community-driven data innovation across the region.
